name: Harvard Electroencephalography Database (HEEDB)

repo.host: Brain Data Science Platform (bdsp.io), AWS Open Data

access.steps: Credentialed BDSP account, sign the DUA, then access via AWS (setup steps on bdsp.io).

cohort.types: all EEG indications (routine, EMU, ICU), not epilepsy-only

modalities: Scalp EEG, 284,341 recordings (median 2 per patient) + clinical reports, ICD-10, medications, notes
size: Not stated in the paper (hundreds of TB scale)
labels: EEG reports for 73% of patients; NLP-extracted findings; informal technician annotations
caveats: Scalp EEG only: no localisation ground truth
Covers all EEG indications (routine, EMU, ICU), not only epilepsy
Patient count in text is '>108,000' / '>100,000'; the four site counts sum to 109,177
checks: Full text PMC12455399 (BDSP landing page not opened; access is credentialed).
pipeline: Population prior and scale: report text + EEG pairs to ground an LLM agent's clinical reasoning, and to pretrain an EEG encoder. Not a virtual-brain input.
key_claim: 284k clinical scalp EEGs from ~109k patients with reports and EHR, behind a BDSP credentialed DUA.

evidence.quote: HEEDB aggregates more than 280 000 EEG recordings from more than 108 000 patients across four Harvard‐affiliated hospitals.
HEEDB is classified as “restricted access,” allowing only credentialed researchers who meet specific criteria.
